drafted_from: tool:write-a-message-body-from-a-document row in tools/send-messages/tool-rows.json, do-work/composition_mail_serializer.py and test/test_composition_mail_serializer.py
start_here: Say to your AI: "Turn my draft update, a heading, two paragraphs and a chart picture, into an HTML and plain-text message body I can send." It writes a request file from the document, runs the serializer on your computer and hands you body_html, body_text and the pictures to attach.
no_lists_because: It names no list: it reads one request file holding a document and writes one result file, with no provider and no stored rows.
instructions: 1. Write the request file {document_nodes: [{id, kind, props, children, visible}] (or one root node), options?} from the document you wrote: headings, paragraphs, images, and blocks marked props.quote for a quoted reply.

2. Say "Turn this document into a message body"; your AI reads the row with tools:list and runs `python3 -I tools/send-messages/do-work/composition_mail_serializer.py request.json body.json` from the Workshop checkout.

3. Read the one summary line (the HTML and text sizes, the number of parts and of degraded blocks) and the output file {body_html, body_text, inline_refs, degraded}; hand body_html and body_text to the sending tool as html and text, and the inline_refs as the pictures to attach.

4. Tell the person about every entry in degraded (a block kind it did not know, shown as its text); map your own block kinds with options.kind_renderers (paragraph, heading1 to heading3 or media); hidden blocks are skipped.

worked_examples.title: A heading, a paragraph with symbols, a picture and a closing line
worked_examples.ask: Turn my update draft into a message body.
